status: PROPOSED — awaiting Product Owner sign-off (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Default goal: lose fat, keep muscle
new_rules.statement: For adults 30+ the default goal is 'Lose fat, keep muscle'; every other goal stays selectable. Aerobic minutes are the main fat-loss lever and strength training protects muscle; HIIT counts as aerobic minutes but is never presented as a fat-loss accelerator. The app shows a realistic expectation: without changing what you eat, about 2–3 kg and a 2–5 cm smaller waist over a few months at 150–300 min/week, and it never promises faster loss. No food or calorie features. Anyone can turn weight features off (no weight or waist tracking, expectations or rate check-in; the default goal becomes general fitness). With pregnancy, or cancer in active treatment, the fat-loss goal is not offered and weight features are off; after giving birth it is not the default and can be chosen from 12 weeks.
new_rules.uncertainty: Default goal and the age-30 threshold are product decisions (D-060). Weight and body-fat effects are GRADE moderate, waist high (Jayedi 2024); effects are trial totals over 8+ weeks, not weekly rates; no RCT shows exercise prevents regain. The weight-features opt-out protects people for whom weight focus is unhelpful without asking about eating disorders (Expert Practice).
new_rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Weekly activity target
new_rules.statement: Weekly target in equivalent minutes (PH-001 accounting: Z1 + 2 × Z2/Z3 work, brisk walks per STEP-002): 200–300 for ages 30–59, 180–250 for 60–64, 150–250 for 65+, never below 150. The target is approached from last week's minutes at ≤ +15%/week (AER-003), ≤ +12%/week at 65+ (AGE-001 × 0.8); steady Z1 work, mostly walking, is the base.
new_rules.uncertainty: Linear benefit to 300 min/week is from trials of 8+ weeks; the lower ceilings from 60 are Expert Practice (recovery and time), not evidence that older adults need less.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Training mix by age band
new_rules.statement: The weekly mix for the fat-loss goal changes with age: strength stays at 3 days by default (2 minimum) in every band; steady Z1 cardio stays at 150–200 min; tempo (Z2) and intervals shrink with age and become low-impact only from 50; a power-emphasis slot (light load lifted fast, low impact) is added from 50; balance work starts at 50 and becomes ≥3 multicomponent days at 65+. Interval sessions need a base of regular training first, longer with age.

30-39.impact_needs: BMI < 30 and no lower-limb pain; ≤1 impact session/week (CON-004)

40-49.impact_needs: BMI < 30 and no lower-limb pain; ≤1 impact session/week (CON-004)

parameters.third_hiit_session_only_under: HIIT-001 (intermediate or advanced, FULL day, no fatigue signal or workload flag, conditioning block)
parameters.hiit_gate_bmi_gte_30_or_age_gte_60: standard screening and low-impact modalities only

new_rules.uncertainty: No trial compares age-banded exercise mixes. Floors (≥2 strength days, ≥3 multicomponent days at 65+, 150 min) are High Evidence; the band cut-points, tempo and HIIT tapers and base lengths are Expert Practice. HIIT safety data come from supervised settings.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Fat-loss year
new_rules.statement: For the fat-loss goal the 12-month sequence is Calibrate(2) → Foundation → Build → Conditioning → Strength → Build II → Conditioning II → Athletic (low-impact power and conditioning) → Consolidation → Review(+2 flex). Every block keeps the FL-003 strength days and aerobic minutes; conditioning blocks shift gym time toward aerobic work without dropping below 2 strength days.
new_rules.uncertainty: Sequence is a coaching design; combined aerobic + resistance training gives the best body-composition result in trials, but block order is untested.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Progress measures without food tracking
new_rules.statement: Waist and strength are the main progress measures; weight is secondary. Waist (optional): every 2–4 weeks, midway between the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone, standing, after a normal breath out, three readings averaged; South Asian reference lines (≥90 cm men, ≥80 cm women) shown as information only. Weight (optional): daily or weekly under the same conditions; the app shows a 7-day mean and judges only 4-week trends. If the 7-day mean falls more than 1 kg/week for 3 weeks in a row, a neutral check-in suggests checking with a doctor if the user isn't trying to diet or feels unwell. No food advice.

parameters.waist_site: midpoint lowest rib – top of iliac crest (WHO STEPS)

new_rules.uncertainty: Daily vs weekly weighing is equivalent (Moderate); averaging, the rate flag and the measuring site are Expert Practice. The Indian consensus measures just above the hip bone, not at the WHO midpoint; readings differ between sites.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-003 / D-060: default goal 'Lose fat, keep muscle' for adults 30+ with an age-banded training mix (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Daily step target
new_rules.statement: Daily step target by age band — 9,000 (30–49), 8,000 (50–59), 7,500 (60–64), 7,000 (65+) — reached gradually: baseline = median of the first 7 valid days (≥500 steps recorded); each week the target rises by p × last week's mean (p = 0.15 under 50, 0.10 from 50), rounded to 50 steps, between 250 and a cap (1,000 under 50, 750 at 50–59, 500 at 60–64, 400 at 65+), only if the target was met on ≥5 of 7 days; held at 3–4 days; lowered by one step after 2 weeks with ≤2 days met; no rise in a deload week or with a lower-limb pain flag; never above the band target.
new_rules.uncertainty: Targets come from observational mortality plateaus (8,000–10,000 under 60, 6,000–8,000 from 60) measured with research devices, not phones. The progression rate is Expert Practice; adaptive goals have Limited Evidence. Steps alone barely change weight (~0.05 kg/week).
new_rules.change_reason: CR-005 / D-062: phone step counter (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Brisk walks count as easy cardio
new_rules.statement: Only brisk-walk bouts — at least 10 minutes in a row at 100 steps/min or more, from the phone's step counter or logged by the user — count as Z1 minutes for PH-001, FL-002 and the AER-003 growth limit. All other steps count only toward the step target, so walking is never counted twice.
new_rules.uncertainty: Cadence threshold Moderate (Tudor-Locke 2011); the 10-minute bout rule is Expert Practice. Whether the phone sensor gives per-minute cadence offline is an engineering check for Part 3.

new_rules.title: Health-condition profiles
new_rules.statement: Users may select health conditions from a versioned table (health_conditions v1.0). Each entry sets conservative limits on general fitness training: doctor's OK advice, highest zone, intervals, minimum reps in reserve, no training to failure, impact, exercise tags to avoid, joint limits, extra warm-up and cool-down, positions, prompts and condition-specific stop signs. With several conditions each control takes its most restrictive value. Control status is self-reported (not sure = not under control); the app never reads or thresholds clinical values (blood pressure, glucose, ketones). A doctor's OK is the user's statement of scope (light–moderate, vigorous, intervals) and unlocks only that scope. Prompts never name a medicine, dose, value target or diagnosis, and never claim to treat a condition. A clinician and a regulatory adviser review the table before any public release.
new_rules.uncertainty: Benefit of exercise is High Evidence for type 2 diabetes, knee/hip osteoarthritis, high blood pressure and pregnancy; nearly every numeric cap is an Expert Practice translation of guideline intensity into app controls. Stroke, COPD and cancer entries rest on less-verified sources. Not a medical device feature: no diagnosis, no clinical values, no treatment claims (D-058).
new_rules.change_reason: CR-001 / D-058: health-condition picker driven by data (Research Update 1.1)

new_rules.title: Starting from your own numbers
new_rules.statement: A user may enter, per exercise, a recent set (weight × reps and reps in reserve) or a best lift (counted as 0 reps in reserve). An estimated 1RM comes from INT-004 only when the entry is valid (reps + RIR ≤ 12, RIR ≤ 3); the first working load is the INT-005 load from 90% of that estimate (CAL-001 known-weights start). If the user last did the exercise 14–27 days ago the estimate is reduced 10%, 28–55 days 20%, and from 56 days the entry is used only as a ceiling for a normal CAL-001 ramp (age 60+ or a flagged screen moves one band longer, as REG-004). The first session confirms it with the CAL-001 rules.
new_rules.uncertainty: e1RM formula accuracy is Moderate (INT-004); the 90% start and the age reductions follow existing CAL-001/REG-004 values rather than direct evidence for self-reported numbers, which may be optimistic.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-002 / D-059: starting weights and personal records

new_rules.title: Planning prompt
new_rules.statement: Optional and under 30 seconds: when the week is planned (or once at onboarding, editable), each training day gets a 'when' (day and time) and an optional 'after what' cue (e.g. after dropping the kids), and the user picks one if-then backup from a short list — e.g. 'If I'm short on time → the express session (ADH-004)'; 'If I miss the planned day → the next free day (REG-002)'. Same weekdays are suggested by default. Never nags; stored on the phone only.
new_rules.uncertainty: Planning helps physical activity in general (Moderate), but delivered online only the effect was not significant (Peng 2022: SMD 0.14, CI −0.02 to 0.31); low cost and no plausible harm.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-006 / D-064: expert review of creator resources suggested by the Product Owner (Research Update 1.1, reviews C and D)

new_rules.title: Calm mobility session
new_rules.statement: An optional 15–30-minute calm mobility session with original content: 2–3 min easy movement, slow flowing mobility for hips, upper back, shoulders and ankles, standing balance holds, holds of 30–60 s, and 3–5 min of easy slow breathing to finish (no breath holds, no special ratios). Offered — never imposed — on rest days as an alternative to MOB-005, on LIGHT and RECOVERY days (RDY-004), and when the check-in stress item is 1–2 (RDY-001). It does not count as Z1 minutes (PH-001, FL-002) or as a strength day; its balance holds count toward FL-003 balance minutes. All SAF-010 tags, joint limits and the SAF-003 pain protocol apply; no heated rooms. Wording says 'for mobility, balance and winding down' and never claims treatment, detox, weight loss or faster recovery.
new_rules.uncertainty: Benefits (flexibility, balance, sleep quality, perceived stress) are moderate vs inactivity and small vs other exercise; trials are small and often unblinded. Format, triggers and dose are Expert Practice. Yoga is light activity (~2.5 METs), has no effect on weight, and stretching does not speed recovery — hence the wording limits.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-006 / D-064: expert review of creator resources suggested by the Product Owner (Research Update 1.1, reviews C and D)

new_rules.title: Training away from the gym today
new_rules.statement: One tap sets today's equipment to the user's saved home kit (bodyweight only by default); the generator then substitutes as usual (SUB-001/002). Strength uses the BW-001 ladders at the plan's RIR. Conditioning defaults to no-jump bodyweight circuits; jumping only under the FL-003 / CON-004 conditions; beginners use 1:2 work:rest (HIIT-002); a circuit at CR10 ≥7 for ≥8 min counts as HIIT (HIIT-001). The warm-up floor applies even to short sessions (WU-003); 20–30-minute express versions are offered (ADH-004). If the home day cannot cover a movement pattern, the weekly check reports the shortfall (PAT-001).
new_rules.uncertainty: Home training improves fitness and strength (Moderate; home HIIT ≈ continuous training; older adults gain strength, power and balance). The preset itself is a Product Rule and its format Expert Practice. Jump-based home intervals were tested in young, lean adults, and plyometric safety data come from supervised programmes.
new_rules.change_reason: CR-006 / D-064: expert review of creator resources suggested by the Product Owner (Research Update 1.1, reviews C and D)

changed_rules.statement: Mostly Z1 and ≤150 prescribed gym minutes/week in strength-emphasis blocks. For the fat-loss goal, brisk walks (STEP-002) are outside this cap.
changed_rules.reason: Fat-loss targets of 200–300 min/week (FL-002) would otherwise clash with the cap; walking adds little interference with strength gains (Research Update 1.1).

changed_rules.statement_add: ≥60: weekly strength volume never drops to the VOL-003 maintenance level; weeks that would plan maintenance (Conditioning and Review blocks, PER-005 holiday or maintenance weeks) use the block-start level instead (beginner 6, intermediate 8, advanced 10 sets per muscle), still over ≥2 exposures (FREQ-002). Deload weeks (DEL-003) are unchanged.
changed_rules.confidence_note: Direction Limited Evidence (one RCT: reduced doses kept muscle gains in 20–35-year-olds but not in 60–75-year-olds); the block-start value is Expert Practice.
changed_rules.reason: Review C (P1). Protects the 'keep muscle' aim of FL-001; the fat-loss year has two Conditioning blocks.

changed_rules.statement: Lift through full range by default. When pain (SAF-003), a limitation tag or a SAF-010 entry restricts range, use the largest pain-free range; where either end could be kept, keep the part where the target muscle is lengthened. A reduced-range set still counts as a hard set (VOL-001).
changed_rules.confidence_note: 'A reduced range costs little muscle growth': Moderate Evidence. 'Prefer the lengthened end': Limited Evidence. Full range stays the default.
changed_rules.reason: Review C (P2). SAF-003 and SAF-010 limit range but no rule said which part to keep.

changed_rules.statement_add: A 'Welcome back' micro-achievement is earned by the first completed session after a missed planned session; one neutral nudge on the next planned day ('Ready when you are; today's plan is set'); no penalty, guilt or streak-loss wording (COACH-001); ADH-001 freeze logic unchanged.
changed_rules.confidence_note: Limited Evidence: in a 61,293-person gym megastudy the best programme rewarded returning after a missed workout, but with incentives; a non-monetary badge is a weaker, untested analogue and effects fade.

changed_rules.statement: 20–30-min express session always available. Habit messaging gives a range, never a fixed day count: for many people a routine starts to feel automatic after about two months, but it varies a lot (from a few weeks to most of a year) and exercise often takes longer; a missed day doesn't undo it.
changed_rules.reason: Review D (P1): medians of 59–66 days with a range of 4–335 (Singh 2024); gym habits take months (Buyalskaya 2023). Review C (P6): single-set sessions still built muscle (Hermann 2025), supporting the express session.

changed_rules.statement_add: A short bone-loading block from the osteoporosis condition entry (≤5 min, low-level landings such as heel drops or small hops, ≥50 landings) is not an impact session under this rule.
changed_rules.reason: SAF-010 osteoporosis entry: the UK consensus advises moderate impact most days; the weekly impact-session cap was written for jumping conditioning work.

changed_rules.statement: Equivalent minutes = Z1 (including STEP-002 brisk walks) + 2 × (Z2 + Z3 work); target ≥150/week; muscle-strengthening ≥2 days.
changed_rules.reason: Defines 'optional logged walking' so steps are never counted twice.

changed_rules.statement: 11 required, 9 optional items; listed exclusions never collected; all data on-device.
changed_rules.note: Waist is already covered by 'body_measurements'. 'third_party_steps_v1' stays excluded: steps come only from this phone's own sensor. Health conditions are sensitive data: on the phone only, in the encrypted backup, deletable.

pending_product_owner_decision.question: Make the excluded cardio machines a per-user choice?
pending_product_owner_decision.proposal: MOD-001 2.0.0: treadmill walking (including incline walking), stationary and air bikes, and stair machines become user-selectable exclusions instead of global ones. Your own profile keeps today's exclusions (treadmill running, stationary bikes, stair machines). Treadmill running stays excluded by default for the fat-loss goal (impact).
pending_product_owner_decision.why: The exclusions came from your personal equipment list (Part 0). For a market-ready weight-loss app for 30+, incline treadmill walking and bikes are the most common joint-friendly cardio; without them, low-impact intervals rely on rower, SkiErg, elliptical and sled only.
